done_when: Workers are told to run only the change's related tests before they stop: forge.toml's fast_test with {base} as the merge base with the default branch, or the test command when the repo has no fast_test; the commit nudge names that same command; CI keeps running the full suite. New and existing repos: every repo gets the instruction from the new release's brief and its next forge sync; a repo without fast_test behaves as today. One command-level test: the commit nudge in a repo with fast_test names the fast command with the base filled in.

findings.body: The new instruction does not replace all full-suite instructions workers receive. Both `.codex/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md:149` and `.claude/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md:149` still require running forge.toml's `test` command before stopping, while this paragraph requires workers changing tests to use that skill. `src/forge/review.py:44–48` ships that requirement to both hosts on sync. Existing conversations also bypass this updated paragraph: `src/forge/worker.py:388–397` returns a continued prompt saying the earlier brief still applies. A conversation started before the upgrade therefore retains the old full-suite requirement; if the worker commits normally, it receives no updated commit nudge. Align the shipped test-audit guidance and send the current related-test instruction in continued rounds so new and existing workers receive the promised behavior.
findings.title: Not done: Workers are told to run only the change's related tests before they stop: forge.toml's fast_test with {base} as the merge base

findings.body: The added test checks only the commit nudge in a manually configured `repo = "forge-source"` repository. It never initializes a client repo, upgrades or syncs a repo adopted on the previous release, or asserts the related-test instruction in the initial worker brief and synced guidance. Reverting the brief and skill changes would leave this test passing. Existing adoption and upgrade tests do not assert this new instruction either (for example, `tests/test_live_adopt.py:67` checks only that the skill exists, and `tests/test_upgrade_command.py:501–504` checks upgrade guidance). Add independent assertions through the real commands for new and previously adopted client repos, as the repository's review rule requires.
findings.title: Not done: Test related-test instructions in new and previously adopted client repos

why: Every worker round runs the repo's whole test suite on the developer's machine before finishing, about 15-20 minutes of each 30-minute round, though CI runs the same full suite again
